correctness.rationale: The outside-neighbor counts in RESULT.md lines 31–50 exhaust all forts by original count and apex membership; in particular a lone original without the apex requires at least n−1 clones, hence contains a clone triple at n=4 as well. Every listed type has no proper fort subset by the same exhaustive classification. A white fort persists, and any stalled nonempty white set is a fort. Counting fort-free complements by apex membership gives the stated polynomial. In the minimum exchange graph the no-apex classes are off-diagonal pairs of Johnson 2-subsets: overlap one costs two moves to the removed diagonal, and swapping to the apex adds one move rather than the two allowed for disjoint pairs. The apex class has (n−3)+2(n−3)+(n−1) moves. The three-coordinate routing through a temporary two-subset is valid since J(n,2) minus any one vertex is connected for n≥4; the apex class attaches to it. Handshaking recovers the edge count. A separate chronological forcing, exhaustive forts, and exchange check at n=4,5,6 found 42,120,270 minimum sets and 150,690,2130 exchange edges. This is bounded corroboration, not the all-n proof.
